‘Staying calm helps me make the right decisions’: Yash Dhull
 There is a philosophical bent to the way Yash Dhull speaks about the game and its uncertainties.
 Published - November 17, 2026 12:05 pm IST - INDORE 
 S. Prasanna Venkatesan READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Delhi batsman Yash Dhull plays a shot against Punjab during the Syed Mushtaq Ali Cricket Tournament in Indore
 | Photo Credit: R.V. Moorthy
 At 24, Yash Dhull sounds wise beyond his years. Perhaps it has something to do with an unexpected health scare when he underwent surgery to repair a congenital hole in his heart. Perhaps it is also the journey cricket has taken him on: from leading India to the U-19 World Cup title and producing impressive First-Class performances, to struggling to establish himself in the IPL and going unsold at the 2026 auction.
 There is, at least, a philosophical bent to the way he speaks about the game and its uncertainties. He frequently punctuates his thoughts with a “touchwood,” as though unwilling to take anything for granted.
 Paliwal, Dhull hit centuries in draw “I have a routine for my matches. I visualise myself in specific situations that I might face. I also make sure to spend some time alone, perhaps by going for a walk. This helps me analyse things better. When you are on your own, you start discovering new things. So, yes, that really helps.
 “I work more on the mental side of things. Staying calm while playing helps me make the right decisions,” he said after his unbeaten 78 off 40 balls (7x4, 5x6) in Delhi’s 109-run win over Punjab in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) on Monday.
 That calm showed in his assured knock. He simply guided even a rogue yorker to the third-man boundary for four. “That was instinctive,” he said.
 IPL auction disappointment
 The disappointment of going unsold at the IPL auction has given Dhull reason to reflect. Spending time with contemporaries Anuj Rawat and Arpit Rana, and talking things through with them, helped him move on “rather than feel stuck.” He believes he needs to produce more match-winning performances, and a new role at No. 3 has offered him an opportunity to put that resolve into practice.
 “Well, ups and downs are part of life. It’s crucial to learn from them and adapt quickly because cricket has become very fast-paced, and in a format like T20, you need to play match-winning innings.
 “Our team’s plan was for the top order to take it as deep as possible, and fortunately, that worked out well. I’ve also taken on a new role at No. 3, and I’m really enjoying it. My goal is to play match-winning knocks for the team,” he said.
